svg.title: Install RHEL 9 and create learner — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Install RHEL 9 and create learner
TLS-APP01 · RHEL 9 installer console
RED HAT ENTERPRISE LINUX 9 — INSTALLATION SUMMARY
Installation Destination: new 30 GB virtual disk only
Software Selection: Minimal Install
Network & Host Name: adapter On / tls-app01.lab.example.test
User Creation: learner [✓] Make this user administrator
Begin Installation
After reboot: text login → learner → password → Bash prompt
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
A text prompt such as [learner@tls-app01 ~]$ appears. A minimal server does not have a GNOME
desktop.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. In VMware Library, double-click TLS-APP01 and click Power on this virtual machine. Click inside its
screen; press Ctrl+Alt to release the mouse when needed.
2. Select Install Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and press Enter. Choose your language, then Continue.
3. On Installation Summary, open Installation Destination. Select only the new 30 GB virtual disk,
choose Automatic, and click Done. No physical Windows disk should appear.
4. Open Software Selection, choose Minimal Install, and click Done. Open Network & Host Name, turn the
adapter On, enter tls-app01.lab.example.test, click Apply, then Done.
5. Open User Creation. Enter learner as the user name, choose Make this user administrator, set your own
strong password, and click Done. Configure the root account as required by the installer; we will sign
in as learner and use sudo.
6. Click Begin Installation, wait, then Reboot System. If the installer reopens, disconnect the ISO in
VMware CD/DVD settings, not the VM disk.
7. At the text login prompt, type learner and press Enter. Type your password and press Enter. Password
characters stay invisible.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
